title: The harvest's tenth
hookLine: a tenth of rain-watered crops, a twentieth of irrigated ones

cards: Two fields, side by side, the same wheat in each. On the first, the farmer did almost nothing for the water. Clouds came over, rain fell, the ground drank, and the wheat came up.
On the second, the farmer had to work for every drop: a well, a bucket, an animal turning a wheel, hour after hour. Harvest day comes for both. Same crop, same weight in the barn.
Does the second farmer owe the same as the first? The answer in the hadith is no, and the reason is in the sky.

teach.h: A TENTH, OR HALF A TENTH.
teach.b: First, the rule. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Umar, says that on what is watered by the rain or by springs, or draws its own water, the share is a tenth.
On what is watered by drawing water, the share is half a tenth. A tenth, or a twentieth. The Arabic word for that tenth is 'ushr.
Second, the reason, as scholars explain it. The first farmer's water came free, from the sky. The second paid for his, in labor and cost.
So the share follows the gift: where more was simply given, more is given back. That's why your line is rain's share. The extra in the first field's due is, in a sense, the rain's part.
The Qur'an tells farmers to give the due on the day of the harvest. No year to wait. And a threshold applies here too, given in loads of grain in the same report you met with the nisab.
Fourth, set this week's pieces side by side. Zakat, the word that means to purify and to grow. Who pays: from their rich, to their poor.
The threshold, below which a person is protected.
One in forty for savings. The year of moons. Four kinds of wealth.
And today, the field: a tenth or a twentieth, depending on the rain. Read together, the rules ask one question in different ways: what was received, and how much of it came without anyone's doing?

how: Muslim farmers whose harvest passes the threshold give a tenth of rain-fed crops and a twentieth of irrigated crops at harvest time, following the hadith of Ibn Umar.

o: a tenth of rain-fed crops, or a twentieth if watered by hand
a tenth of a farm's land, set aside for the poor
one fortieth of a harvest, the same as for savings

games.q: the harvest's tenth — tap the pairs.

s: every crop owes the same share, however it was watered
rain or springs: a tenth. water drawn by labor: half a tenth.
a threshold applies to the harvest too
the same report you met with the nisab gives it in loads of grain.
the hadith on the tenth and the twentieth is in Sahih al-Bukhari

games.q: you're the second farmer. you hauled every drop from a well all season. harvest day: what share does the hadith ask of you?
o: a tenth, the same as the rain-fed field.
nothing, because you worked for it.
games.why: half a tenth. your labor is counted, so the share is smaller. the rain-fed field gives more, because more was given to it.

practice: In Sahih al-Bukhari, when the Prophet ﷺ saw rain, he would ask for it to be a beneficial rain: allahumma sayyiban nafi'an. If you pray, you can say those words now, or simply alhamdulillah.
If you don't, remember the last rain you heard, the sound on a window, the smell of the street afterward, and follow it into soil, into wheat, into the bread you ate this week.

wordCard.voice: The harvest's tenth. 'Ushr: a tenth of rain-watered crops, a twentieth of crops watered by labor, given on the harvest day. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the tenth, the share of a rain-watered harvest.

carryVoice: Your line: rain's share. Next, the other side of the ledger: who receives it. A week of zakat, done.
